newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: City of Geneva pledges funds for new Swiss airline.
newsitem.headline: City of Geneva pledges funds for new Swiss airline.

text.p: The city of Geneva on Monday pledged funds for a new airline that will fill the gap left by national carrier Swissair's controversial decision last year to switch most of its long-haul flights to Zurich.

The head of Geneva's cantonal government, Jean-Philippe Maitre, told news agency ATS the city would contribute five million Swiss francs to Swiss World Airways (SWA). SWA, with start-up capital of 60 million Swiss francs, will begin long- distance flights this year from Geneva's Cointrin airport serving western Switzerland and Alpine France.

The airline was set up after Swissair stopped most of its loss-making, long-haul flights from Geneva in favour of the Zurich hub, a decision that drew strong criticism from French-speaking Switzerland. Swissair executives say the country cannot afford two international airports.

The international city of Geneva is home to the United Nation's European headquarters and key agencies. Many Western corporations have European headquarters in the city, which is also the hub of Switzerland's private banking industry.

SWA plans to serve destinations such as New York, Washington, Boston, Chicago and Montreal. It wants financial guarantees of 15 million to 20 million Swiss francs from cantonal governments in French-speaking Switzerland.
